title: Invertible leading pivot for a finite free map with residue kernel dimension one
statement: Let R and A be commutative rings with an R-algebra structure on the local ring A. Let f : X → Y be an R-linear map. Suppose A ⊗_R X and A ⊗_R Y are finite free and the kernel of κ(A) ⊗_R f is isomorphic to κ(A). There exist A-modules U,C, with C free, coordinate equivalences A ⊗_R X ≃ U × A and A ⊗_R Y ≃ U × C, and an automorphism B of U, such that the first coordinate of f(u,0) is B(u). The off-diagonal and lower-right blocks are unrestricted.

proof.text: Choose finite bases and identify reduction of the scalar-extended matrix with the given residue map using tensor associativity. Rank-nullity shows that the source dimension n is positive and the matrix rank is n-1.

Choose independent columns and then rows forming a nonzero (n-1)-square residue minor. Its determinant lifts to a unit in A. Permute the chosen columns first, the single remaining column last, and the selected rows first with their complement last. Set U to A^(n-1) and C to the complementary coordinate module, which is free.

The selected square matrix defines an automorphism B, with inverse the adjugate times the inverse of its unit determinant. Evaluating the first component on (u,0) gives B(u). For n=1 the minor is empty with determinant 1; U=0 and B is the identity. This step does not eliminate any off-diagonal block.
